records.abstract: Twinning rates in developed countries have recently registered an increase. records.abstract: There is widespread concern about a possible decline in human fertility in recent decades. The spontaneous dizygotic twinning rate provides a way of measuring a combination of male plus female fertility as it reflects the frequency of double ovulation, the probability of fertilization, and the survival of the zygote. records.abstract: Historically, mothers producing twins gave birth, on average, more often than non-twinners. records.abstract: The present study examines secular changes in the rate of twinning in Denmark during the period of 1931-77. records.abstract: Since the 1970s, twin birth rates have increased sharply in developed countries. This article aims to estimate the twinning rate in sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries throughout 1986-2016 and analyze its spatial, temporal, and ethnic variations. records.abstract: Trends of twinning rates were analyzed using vital statistics in Austria, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Canada, Australia, Hong Kong, Israel, Japan, and Singapore during the period from 1972 to 1996. records.abstract: The hypothesis of seasonality of twin births was investigated in two important maternity hospitals in the State of São Paulo, Brazil. No evidence of seasonality has been detected either for the twin birth rate considered as a whole or for dizygotic twinning rate. records.title: Constant multiple birth rates in the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic until recently, 1972–1995
records.abstract: Using vital statistics, yearly changes in the twinning and triplet rates by zygosity were investigated in the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic during the period 1972-1995. Monozygotic (MZ) twinning rates in both countries had remained nearly constant (about 3 per 1000 total births) during that period. With a few exceptions, the dizygotic (DZ) twinning rates remained constant from 1972 to 1994, and increased in 1995 for both countries. MZ twinning rates for both countries were the lowest in Europe.
